result.title: Find your purpose after major setbacks: Katie Piper on how to adapt, reinvent and lead
result.description:
What do you do when life changes in an instant—and the future you envisioned disappears? Advocate and author Katie Piper explains how she rebuilt her life after surviving an acid attack at 24 driven by a man she'd briefly dated, founded a burn-rehabilitation charity and reframed “Why me?” as “What now?” It’s a special conversation about resilience, personal reinvention and leading through adversity.

You’ll learn:
-Why real confidence comes from knowing you can adapt and recover
-How the ease of a modern world can make us less able to embrace challenge for growth
-How to see challenge as a way to recommit to your purpose
-How acceptance, discomfort and a self-authored identity can help you start again
-Why vulnerability and empathy are strengths in leadership
Katie Piper OBE is a bestselling author, television presenter and founder of the Katie Piper Foundation, which supports burn survivors through rehabilitation. Her documentary, 'Katie: My Beautiful Face', was nominated for a BAFTA in 2010. She is also a survivor of male violence and an advocate for people with burns and visible differences.
This conversation explores resilience, purpose, trauma recovery, inclusive leadership and turning pain into purpose. Follow Meet the Leader on YouTube, Spotify or podcast apps, and subscribe for more conversations with people shaping the world

This interview was recorded in January 2026 at the World Economic Forum’s Annual Meeting in Davos Switzerland.

result.title: Saving Coral Reefs & Are We Ready For El Nino? | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:12 - Are we ready for El Nino?:
While meteorologists don’t yet know exactly how powerful the weather pattern forming in the Pacific will be this time, they are increasingly confident it will be one of the biggest El Niños on record.
So how can business leaders and policy-makers best prepare? Celeste Saulo, Secretary-General of the World Meteorological Organization, offers some insights.Saulo was a guest on Agenda Dialogues, a World Economic Forum podcast. 

03:22 - Saving coral reefs from crisis:
Archireef creates 3D-printed terracotta tiles that give young #corals the best chance of taking root and flourishing. Vriko Yu, Archireef’s Co-Founder and CEO, explains why this is so important, and what solutions like hers need to expand. 

05:49 - This flying boat uses less power than e-bikes:
This battery-powered boat, built by Swiss start-up MobyFly, races along above the surface thanks to hydrofoils - wing-like structures mounted underneath the hull. It’s a fast, quiet and comfortable way to travel, says CEO Sue Putallaz, and because there’s almost no drag, it’s 80% more efficient than traditional watergoing transport.

result.title: How to Focus on What Matters Most: 5 Leaders' Effective Strategies
result.description:
How do you focus on what matters most in a distracted and noisy world? In this special Meet the Leader episode, leading thinkers and adventurers share practical ways to reclaim your attention and sharpen your focus so you can spend your time on the right priorities. Their strategies and approaches will help you refresh your thinking, make better decisions and prevent distraction from turning into burnout.

You’ll learn to:

• Rethink the first and last things you do each day to sharpen your attention
 • Craft a “to-feel list” to clarify priorities and make days more meaningful
 • Better appreciate the present to take control of your attention
 • Think 'like an ancestor' to help you think beyond the short term

Featured voices include human flourishing expert and social psychologist Jonathan Haidt; writer and three-time cancer survivor Suleika Jaouad; blind adventurer Hiro Iwamoto and navigator Doug Smith; Nia Tero CEO Aulani Wilhelm; and Buddhist monk Shoukei Matsumoto. Together, they explore attention management, focus, deep work, reflection, long-term thinking and improving leadership in a distracted world.

Subscribe to Meet the Leader on Apple Podcasts, Spotify or your favorite podcast platform for more practical leadership insights.

result.title: Coral reefs are at crisis point. This scientist has a solution
result.description:
Archireef creates 3D-printed terracotta tiles that give young #corals the best chance of taking root and flourishing. Vriko Yu, Archireef’s Co-Founder and CEO, explains why this is so important, and what solutions like hers need to expand. 

Coral reefs are home to 25% of ocean species, but up to half of these vital marine habitats have already been lost due to warming oceans, pollution and overfishing. This decade still offers a window in which to restore and conserve as many reefs as possible, says Yu.

Vriko Yu is a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader, part of a network of 1,400 people under 40 driving positive change in their communities and beyond. Learn more: https://www.younggloballeaders.org/home

result.title: Why AI Needs Regulation & How Fire Clouds Worsen European Fires | WEF | Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:12 - A philosopher on why AI needs regulation: 
Atoosa Kasirzadeh, philosopher and Assistant Professor at Carnegie Mellon University, explains why she believes an ethical framework must go hand in hand with the development of artificial intelligence.

02:06 - How fire clouds worsen European fires: 
As France and Spain battle terrifying wildfires, experts believe they’ve spotted a phenomenon new to the region: fire clouds. These occur when a wildfire is so large and severe it generates its own weather system, including thunderstorms, which can spread the fire with gusts of wind and even ignite new areas with lightning strikes. 

03:27 - Why are companies interested in Moon dust?: 
Helium-3 is an incredibly precious resource, used to cool quantum computers, supercharge medical imaging - and could even one day enable nuclear fusion. But just a few kilograms are produced on Earth each year, and each kilo is valued at $20 million. There is one place where helium-3 is abundant, though: the Moon. Now start-ups like Interlune are looking to mine this rare resource using autonomous solar-powered robots.
